urn.declaration.description: How a plan artifact declares its own URN.

idiom.route_handler.description: What a boundary handler (route, endpoint) looks like.

idiom.auth_guard.description: How a handler establishes the authenticated principal.

idiom.error_types.description: How domain and boundary errors are typed and raised.

idiom.validation_shape.description: How request input is validated before use.

idiom.external_import.description: How an import of an external package (outside the project graph) is recognised.

idiom.forbidden_runtime_imports.description: Runtime, framework and transport import specifiers that inner roles must not import.

idiom.runtime_globals.description: Runtime globals that count as framework machinery.

idiom.machinery.description: What counts as delivery machinery (server, transport, runtime) in this stack.

idiom.dto_mapper_naming.description: Name patterns of functions that map between DTOs and domain entities.

idiom.control_keywords.description: Control-flow keywords that count toward nesting depth.

idiom.nesting_measure.description: How nesting depth is measured in the stack's syntax.

idiom.destructive_request.description: The declarative markup construct that issues a destructive request.

idiom.mutation_requests.description: Declarative markup constructs that issue non-destructive mutating requests.

idiom.confirmation_gate.description: The declarative construct that asks the user to confirm before a request.

idiom.prompt_gate.description: The declarative construct that asks the user for input before a request.

idiom.declaration_scope.description: Where a gate must be declared relative to the request construct.

idiom.comment_marker.description: Line-comment syntax of the stack's source files.

idiom.markup_kinds.description: Artifact kinds (static pages, templates, server-rendered output) that count as markup in which declarative request and gate constructs can appear.

idiom.plan_syntax.description: Constructs of plan artifacts (produce/consume, routes, trains, ownership, status, references, sessions).

idiom.acceptance_schema.description: The acceptance-artifact schema: precondition fields, trigger shapes, assertion kinds, harness templates and codes, telemetry decision.

idiom.docs_syntax.description: Documentation constructs: identity, status and lifecycle, relationships, internal references, generated regions, decision-record headers.

idiom.convention_graph.description: Convention-graph constructs: node id fields, operative fields, anchors, edge endpoints, rule-binding files.

idiom.routing.description: Composition-root routing constructs: action-to-route maps, route tables, journey maps and registries, start and launch surfaces.

idiom.test_constructs.description: Test-code constructs: test case and context, assertions and matchers, substitutions, phase and RED markers, fixtures, browser measurements.

idiom.responsive.description: Responsive styling: breakpoints, viewports, width conditions and declarations, length units, styling contexts and notations.

idiom.design_system.description: Design-system constructs: token definition and reference, raw colour literals, component exports, barrels, interactive controls, renderers.

idiom.markup.description: Declarative markup constructs beyond the dedicated idiom keys: request and swap constructs, progress signals, event handlers, ids, interpolation.

idiom.telemetry.description: Telemetry constructs: emit calls, event shapes, vendor SDKs, observation tiers and channels.

idiom.logging.description: Logging constructs: logger receivers, structured logger, context shape, ad-hoc print calls, CLI output.

idiom.security.description: Security-relevant constructs: SQL sinks and parameterisation, authorization checks, environment access, error-response payloads.

idiom.module_boundaries.description: Module and runtime boundary constructs: imports, outbound I/O calls, servers, collaborators, composition domains, structural roots.

idiom.dto_shape.description: How a DTO is declared, named and kept pure.

idiom.naming.description: Naming constructs: verb lexicon, name-token separators.

idiom.source_syntax.description: Source-syntax facts used by checks: comment-line kinds, complexity measure, runtime-declaration header and values.

idiom.collaboration.description: Collaboration-toolchain idioms: seat addresses, integration branches, delegation context, model portfolio, file-reading tool.

enforcement.runner.description: The command or tool that runs the stack's convention checks.

enforcement.default_disposition.description: The disposition of a rule that does not declare one.

enforcement.suppression_marker.description: Syntax of a time-boxed suppression of one rule.

enforcement.report_location.description: How a finding reports its location.

enforcement.exceptions.description: Where and how intentional exceptions are declared (allow-lists, coverage exceptions, naming exceptions).

enforcement.presets.description: Profile presets per kind of work and the location of each profile's registry.

tooling.package_manager.description: The package manager that owns dependencies.

tooling.lockfile.native.description: Lockfile(s) owned by the package manager.

tooling.lockfile.foreign.description: Lockfiles of other package managers that must not coexist with the native one.

tooling.foreign_install_commands.description: Install commands of other package managers.

tooling.workspace_declaration.description: How the workspace declares its package manager.

tooling.urn_resolver.description: The command that resolves a URN to its artifact.

tooling.commands.description: Helper commands of the stack's toolchain (authoring, plan session, generators, renderers, seat lifecycle, cleanup).

tooling.language_scopes.description: Languages per check scope (scanned code, test files, in-scope files).

tooling.test_harness.description: The declared test harness, foreign harnesses that must not be used, and runtime families of tests.

tooling.typecheck.description: Typecheck configuration, checker dependencies, no-emit commands, step names and strictness options.

tooling.stack_signals.description: Markers by which a repository or package is recognised as this stack.

tooling.appendix_formats.description: Appendix types, their file formats, and which formats the agent tooling can read.
